steps.prompt: In our base-ten system, $345$ means $3 \times 100 + 4 \times 10 + 5$. What do you think $345$ would mean if we counted in sixes instead of tens?

cards.title: Place values in base b
cards.body: In base $b$, the places are worth $1, b, b^2, b^3, \ldots$ from the right, and the digits run from $0$ to $b - 1$. So $213_5 = 2 \cdot 25 + 1 \cdot 5 + 3 = 58$. Base $2$ (binary) uses only $0$ and $1$.

try.prompt: What is the value of the place for the digit $2$ in $213_5$?

cards.title: Out of base ten
cards.body: To write $n$ in base $b$, take the biggest place value that fits, see how many times it fits, and carry on with what is left. Or divide by $b$ again and again: the remainders, read from last to first, are the digits.

steps.text: The places are $27, 9, 3, 1$. $27$ fits once, leaving $18$.

try.prompt: What is left after taking $27$ from $45$?

cards.title: The common trap: reading it as base ten
cards.body: $213_5$ is NOT two hundred and thirteen. A digit can't be $b$ or more in base $b$: $5$ never appears in base $5$. If a problem says "in some base $b$", write each number as a polynomial in $b$ and solve.

prompts: Explain how you would turn a base-ten number into base $2$ to a friend.
